_comment: Rules for tools/licence-scan.py. Every list stays short and every exemption gives its reason (the scanner refuses to load one without). The allow-list is the project's licence policy: widening it is a maintainer decision, not a contributor's.
_allow: CC-BY-4.0 covers art and presets only (textures, models, sounds, structures, world presets), never code.

wording.why: GNU GPL, LGPL or AGPL licence text: copyleft, not on the allow-list
GNU LGPL licence text: copyleft, not on the allow-list
GNU AGPL: network copyleft, not on the allow-list
the Free Software Foundation, named by GPL-family headers
a licence identifier that is not on the allow-list
'All rights reserved' in a header: no permission to copy
a Stack Exchange answer: CC BY-SA, not on the allow-list for code

provenance.why: glibc is LGPL-2.1: its code may not be copied or ported
the IBM 'Ultimate Solution' routines in glibc, LGPL-2.1

permissions._comment: Code used by its author's permission with no open-source licence. A register row says `PERMISSION <name>`; each name says where the permission is recorded. Adding one is the owner's decision; none is recorded yet (CBScript waits on #142).

exempt.why: the scanner names the rules it enforces
the register names each third-party licence
a third-party licence text kept beside what it covers
a third-party notice kept beside what it covers (each one has a THIRD_PARTY.md row)
the full licence texts of what the jar bundles (each one has a THIRD_PARTY.md row); never source code
the table of what the jar bundles and each component's licence

jar_licences._comment: group:artifact -> licence, for a bundled library whose own POM names none (it inherits it from a parent POM the jar does not carry); each row says where the licence was read.
